title: Elastic–perfectly plastic thick cylinder: plastic zone and collapse pressure
source: Hill, The Mathematical Theory of Plasticity, Oxford 1950, ch. V §2: a von Mises cylinder in plane strain, elastically incompressible, with the plastic zone a ≤ r ≤ c under the pressure p = k (2 ln(c/a) + 1 − c²/b²), k = σ_y/√3, and the bore displacement u_a = k c²/(2 G a); collapse when c = b at p = 2k ln(b/a)

quantities.quantity: bore displacement at the pressure that takes the plastic zone to c = 15 (a = 10, b = 20, σ_y = 250)
quantities.reason: 20 reduced quad8 elements through the wall resolve the logarithmic plastic field and ν = 0.4999 stands in for Hill's incompressible elasticity (0.009 % apart); u_a ∝ c², so 0.2 % on u_a is 0.1 % on the plastic radius

quantities.quantity: radial force on the bore (per radian times 2π, height 1) at a bore displacement of 0.3, 24 times the first yield's: the collapse pressure 2k ln 2 = 200.094 times 2πa
quantities.reason: once the wall is plastic through, perfect plasticity holds the force at the collapse value (σ_θ − σ_r = 2k everywhere, σ_z the mean of the others as plastic flow dominates); the band admits the quadrature of the logarithmic field
